Although overshadowed by the iOS 27 public beta this time, Apple also rolled out a new public beta firmware update for AirPods the same week. This update brings a long-awaited feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ.

AirPods public beta details

The AirPods public beta firmware version is 9.0.314, with build number 9A314b. The following AirPods models can be updated:

  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2 (Lightning and USB-C versions)
  • AirPods 4
  • AirPods 4 (Active Noise Cancellation version)
  • AirPods Max 2

You can opt into the AirPods public beta in the Settings app on your iPhone. When your AirPods are connected, a toggle will appear in the Settings app, allowing you to enable the beta firmware. Afterwards, when your AirPods are placed in the charging case and within range of the paired iPhone, the beta will automatically download and install.

  • Open the Settings app
  • Tap Bluetooth
  • Tap the (i) icon next to your AirPods
  • Scroll down and turn on AirPods Beta Updates

Custom EQ officially lands on AirPods

Once you've installed the AirPods public beta, you'll see a long-awaited new feature in the Settings app: custom EQ.

Thanks to the new custom EQ controls, you can now fine-tune your AirPods' sound performance in greater detail. In the Settings app, you can independently adjust the bass, midrange, and treble of your AirPods.

Apple explains: "AirPods are meticulously designed and engineered by Apple's team to faithfully reproduce the original sound of music, TV shows, movies, and even calls. If you prefer a different sound style, you can customise the audio tone of your AirPods when playing any audio."

While adjusting your custom EQ settings, you can play a song from Apple Music directly in the Settings app to hear the effect of your adjustments in real time.

This is by no means the most advanced equaliser feature on the market — just a basic three-band system. But regardless, it's a feature AirPods users have waited a long time for, and Apple has finally made it available — even though most users will probably end up sticking with the default settings.

You can find this brand-new custom EQ feature under the Audio & Routing menu in the AirPods section of the Settings app. This feature is available on all AirPods equipped with the H2 chip, including AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

Other new features iOS 27 brings to AirPods

Here are the other new features iOS 27 brings to AirPods:

  • Redesigned Settings app: iOS 27 has redesigned the AirPods interface within the Settings app, reorganising the controls into separate categories such as Hearing Health, Find My, and Live Translation.
  • Adaptive Audio slider: The Settings app now features a slider that lets you fine-tune the Adaptive Audio mode in greater detail.
  • GymKit: Although GymKit has been around for years, it has always required an Apple Watch. As my colleague Zac mentioned, iOS 27 brings the complete GymKit experience to iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.
  • Precision Finding: You can now use Precision Finding in the Find My app on your Apple Watch to locate your AirPods Pro 3.
  • Siri AI: When paired with a compatible iPhone, AirPods can interact with Siri AI.

Summary

Which new AirPods feature are you most looking forward to trying? Will you give the new custom EQ a go? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
